subject.title: fix(msteams): escape markup in mention display names

question: Is this PR's loopback send-stack wire capture plus Microsoft Teams documentation sufficient proof for the narrow mention-escaping fix, or should merge wait for live Teams tenant/client render proof?
rationale: OpenClaw policy prefers live verification for external API behavior, but the source contract and loopback wire proof strongly cover the payload-construction bug and the contributor says they cannot provide tenant/client proof.

options.title: Accept contract-level proof
options.body: Treat the Microsoft Teams mention contract, source-level reproduction, jsdom structure check, and loopback send-stack capture as sufficient once CI is green.

options.title: Waive the proof gate
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the local parser and loopback transport proof for this narrow escaping change and proceed with ordinary merge review.

options.title: Pause for Teams owner review
options.body: Keep the PR open for a Teams-area owner to decide whether the remaining client-rendering uncertainty is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept contract-level proof
recommendation.body: Treat the Microsoft Teams mention contract, source-level reproduction, jsdom structure check, and loopback send-stack capture as sufficient once CI is green.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent msteams ownership and release-adjacent work make this the best available owner for the proof-sufficiency choice.
